name: Texas AI governance applicability matrix
disclaimer: This matrix is an engineering artifact, not legal advice. Every row records a citation, a proposed control, and an applicability value that the district's own counsel must set. Rows default to requires_legal_review. Nothing here asserts that deploying this platform makes a district compliant with any statute or rule.
verification_note: capitol.texas.gov and statutes.capitol.texas.gov were unreachable from the build environment (blocked by the network egress proxy), so primary bill text could not be read directly. Rows marked secondary_source_only were derived from law-firm and policy-tracker summaries and MUST be re-verified against primary text before a district relies on them. See docs/governance/source-registry.md.

requirements.source: HB 149 (89R), Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (TRAIGA)
requirements.statute_or_rule: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code ch. 552 (AI provisions; TRAIGA spans ch. 551-554)
requirements.actor: developer or deployer of an AI system
requirements.summary: TRAIGA restricts developing or deploying AI for enumerated prohibited purposes, reported to include behavioural manipulation toward self-harm or crime, incitement, certain governmental social scoring, specified biometric identification without consent, infringement of constitutional rights, unlawful discrimination, and covered sexual-exploitation or CSAM content.
requirements.use_case_applicability: All AI use cases registered in the platform.
requirements.required_control: Prohibited-use screening at use-case registration and a runtime policy check before execution; registration of a use case matching a prohibited category is refused rather than warned about.
requirements.evidence: AI registry record, risk classification, approval record, audit trail of the registration decision.
requirements.notes: The enacted bill was substantially narrowed from the introduced version, with most private-sector obligations removed and the focus shifted toward government use. The exact enumerated categories and their scope must be read from primary text before a district relies on this row.

requirements.statute_or_rule: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code ch. 552 (governmental AI interaction disclosure)
requirements.actor: governmental agency interacting with a consumer via AI
requirements.summary: Reported to require disclosure when a person is interacting with an AI system in specified governmental contexts.
requirements.use_case_applicability: Any use case where a student, parent, or member of the public interacts with the assistant.
requirements.required_control: Per-use-case disclosure configuration, enforced at the gateway; a use case flagged as public-facing cannot be approved without a disclosure string.
requirements.evidence: Disclosure configuration per AI system, screenshots or transcripts showing the disclosure, audit records.
requirements.notes: Whether an independent school district is a 'governmental agency' for this provision is a legal question this repository does not answer. Districts should implement the disclosure regardless as recommended practice -- it is low cost and independently supported by the TACC K-12 guidance.

requirements.statute_or_rule: Amends Tex. Gov't Code ch. 2054 (AI definitions, inventory, heightened scrutiny)
requirements.actor: state agency; local government (as defined in the bill)
requirements.summary: Reported to require state agencies to inventory AI systems and assess risk as part of IT strategic planning, with local governments required to assess high-risk AI systems and share that information with DIR on request. Establishes definitions including 'consequential decision' and 'heightened scrutiny artificial intelligence system', and directs DIR toward a statewide AI code of ethics modelled on the NIST AI RMF.
requirements.use_case_applicability: All district AI systems; heightened-scrutiny classification for systems influencing consequential decisions.
requirements.required_control: Mandatory AI inventory with risk classification, heightened-scrutiny flag, named owners, and review dates; export capability for a DIR information request.
requirements.evidence: AI inventory export, risk assessments, heightened-scrutiny register, review history.
requirements.notes: CRITICAL OPEN QUESTION: whether a Texas ISD falls within this bill's definition of 'local government' determines whether this row is a legal obligation or a recommended practice. The bill's own definition section must be read; do not assume. The platform implements the control either way because an AI inventory is independently justified by NIST AI RMF GOVERN-1.

requirements.summary: Systems that autonomously influence consequential decisions (reported examples include benefit eligibility and licensing) receive heightened scrutiny.
requirements.use_case_applicability: Any use case touching discipline, special education, eligibility, placement, admissions, or employment decisions.
requirements.required_control: Heightened-scrutiny classification blocks autonomous execution and requires a documented human oversight mechanism before approval; the contract refuses to construct such a record without one.
requirements.evidence: Risk classification record, human-oversight description, approval record, human-approval audit events.
requirements.notes: The platform's Phase 0-2 scope deliberately excludes autonomous consequential decisions entirely, which is the strongest available control.

requirements.statute_or_rule: AI and cybersecurity training certification; training requirement for certain state, local government, and school district employees
requirements.actor: DIR (certification); state, local government, and school district employees (completion)
requirements.summary: Reported to require DIR to certify and periodically update AI and cybersecurity training programs, and to require certain state and local government employees AND school district employees to complete such training.
requirements.use_case_applicability: Platform-wide; a governance obligation on district staff rather than on any single use case.
requirements.required_control: Training assignment, completion, certification, and expiration tracking with evidence links and recurring reassignment; reporting on completion rates by role.
requirements.evidence: Per-employee training records, completion dates, certificates, expiration and reassignment history.
requirements.notes: This is the row with the clearest direct hook to school districts: secondary sources state the bill names school district employees explicitly. 'Conditional' rather than 'applies' because which employees are covered, and on what cadence, must be read from primary text and from the DIR certification criteria.

requirements.statute_or_rule: Artificial intelligence division within the Department of Information Resources
requirements.summary: Reported to create an AI division within DIR tasked with helping state agencies and other entities modernise legacy state government computer systems using generative AI.
requirements.use_case_applicability: None as a legal obligation. Retained as a product capability.
requirements.required_control: Before/after measurement of AI-assisted processes: baseline time, cost, and resources against AI-assisted equivalents, with quality and outcome change.
requirements.notes: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the original handoff framing. HB 2818 is an agency-structure bill creating a DIR division; on the available evidence it does not impose a modernisation-measurement duty on school districts. The platform still implements measurement, because a district needs to demonstrate that AI improved a process -- but it is a product capability and a procurement argument, not a compliance control. Marking it otherwise would be exactly the kind of overclaiming this matrix exists to prevent.

requirements.actor: state agencies; adopted voluntarily by other public entities
requirements.summary: DIR-published acceptable use policy template for AI, covering permitted uses, prohibited uses, data handling, and human review expectations.
requirements.use_case_applicability: All use cases; forms the baseline district AI acceptable use policy.
requirements.required_control: District AI acceptable use policy stored as a versioned policy document, bound to each AI system record via policy_version.
requirements.evidence: Adopted policy document, version history, per-system policy binding, staff acknowledgement records.
requirements.notes: The URL was not fetched from the build environment. Confirm the current published version before adoption.

requirements.source: Texas Education Code and federal FERPA
requirements.statute_or_rule: Student records confidentiality (FERPA, 20 U.S.C. 1232g; Tex. Educ. Code ch. 26)
requirements.summary: Student education records are confidential and disclosable only to those with a legitimate educational interest or other lawful basis.
requirements.use_case_applicability: Any use case whose corpus includes student records.
requirements.required_control: Trust-domain separation of student-confidential content, authorization before retrieval, per-role entitlement requirements beyond role membership, and full retrieval audit.
requirements.evidence: Authorization decision audit records, retrieval audit records, passing access-boundary test suite.
requirements.notes: This row is included because it is the obligation most likely to be tested in practice, and it is the one the platform's architecture is most directly shaped by. It predates every 89R AI bill.
